short_description: Consumer-facing physical trait that reports a cautious panel-relative signal related to BMI-adjusted waist-to-hip ratio tendency within the current local reference panel.
summary_note: Usable consumer-facing physical trait with strong raw-array support and a clearer interpretation boundary between inherited body-fat-distribution tendency and current measured waist and hip proportions beyond overall BMI for the no-imputation workflow.
what_it_measures: A panel-relative polygenic signal associated with BMI-adjusted waist-to-hip ratio tendency, calibrated within the current local empirical reference panel.
interpretation_template: BMI-adjusted waist-to-hip ratio tendency is presented here as a cautious relative body-fat-distribution signal beyond overall body-size tendency, not as a direct tape-measure readout of your current waist and hip measurements. {interpretation}
caution_text: Use as a cautious panel-relative signal only. No imputation or ancestry-adjusted normalization is used, and the output should not be treated as a deterministic real-world result, a direct tape-measure estimate, or medical advice about abdominal fat distribution.
limitations: Percentiles and z-scores are relative to the local reference panel, not to a population-wide benchmark.

The source phenotype is adjusted for BMI, so this trait is best read as a relative body-fat-distribution tendency beyond overall body-size signal rather than as a general statement about total weight or adiposity.

Real-world waist and hip proportions depend strongly on sex, age, hormones, training, nutrition, pregnancy history, illness, and current body composition, so this should not be treated as a precise measurement of present-day body shape.
confidence_note: Confidence reflects overlap and reference robustness under the no-imputation raw-array workflow, not certainty about the real-world trait.
reference_note: Percentiles and z-scores are calibrated against a local empirical reference artifact built from raw-array files in this project; they are panel-relative, not population-wide.
